headline: Signed July taxes-abated list and State Tax Form 147; approved July 28 minutes; discussed Partridge Hill Road reassessments.
summary: A Property Tax Relief Bill from the Mayor of Boston would change the abatement filing deadline from thirty to forty-five days after the due date. Assessors will send letters asking lawmakers to vote against it, saying it would delay setting the tax rate. Properties at 64, 65 and 87 Partridge Hill Road will be reassessed for FY20 through FY26, and the town will ask the State for permission to abate those years.
decisions: Approved the open session and executive session minutes of July 28, 2026, by unanimous vote.
Signed the monthly list of taxes abated for July 2026.
Signed State Tax Form 147 for property tax abatement for active duty in a foreign country.

plain_text:
TOWN OF SUTTON
BOARD OF ASSESSORS
 4 UXBRIDGE ROAD
SUTTON, MA  01590-1702
  508-865-8722
                     Meeting Minutes – August 4, 2026
Present:  Robert Nunnemacher, Chairman
    Matthew Read, Assessor
               Tracey Tardy, Principal Assessor
 
 Meeting called to order at 5:00 p.m.
1.         The Board voted unanimously to accept the open session meeting minutes and executive session
            meeting minutes of July 28, 2026
2.         Old & New Business
The Principal Assessor reviewed with the Board a Property Tax Relief Bill brought forward by the Mayor of Boston
to amend the abatement filing date from thirty days to forty-five days after due date.  Bill is in the Senate now – Assessors
have been asked to send letter to the Senate and House of Representatives to vote against this change as it will delay setting 
the tax rate process
The Board discussed the Mass Electric hearing – the Fiscal Year 2026 we will be requesting a hearing for a dismissal as there
was a late payment
The Principal Assessor spoke to the Department of Local Services (DLS) Representative regarding second homes and
valuations
The Board reviewed a response from attorney on ownership of 38 Main Street and will need to discuss with Town Manager 
how the Town would like to proceed
The Principal Assessor informed the Board that properties at 64, 65 and 87 Partridge Hill Road will all need to be reassessed 
from FY20-FY26 and request permission from the State to abate those years as the properties should have been exempt.  
Principal Assessor spoke to DLS law who recommends this process.
Board discussed small business exemptions (list came in from the State).  Out of 193 counts 143 would be considered small 
business and that would not be advantageous for the Town as we would lose most of the personal property tax.
3.         Decisions & Actions Taken
The Board signed the Monthly List of Taxes Abated for July, 2026
The Board signed State Tax Form 147 – Property Tax Abatement for Active Duty in Foreign Country
4.         Adjourned Open Session @ 5:50 to enter into Executive Session regarding
            Abatements/Exemptions
The Board entered into executive session to review abatement and/or exemption applications pursuant
to Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 59, Section 60, and Chapter 30A, Section 21, Item number 7. We are meeting in executive session 
to comply with Chapter 59, Section 60, which limits inspection of Chapter 59 abatement and exemption applications to assessors and the 
deputies, clerks and assistants of the assessors, and certain other parties listed in the law. Chapter 30A, Section 21, Item number 7 permits 
public bodies to meet in executive session for the purpose of complying with general laws. 
The Board of Assessors adjourned its open meeting at or about 5:50 p.m. 
Respectfully Submitted,
Linda Hicks, Assistant Assessor
